rationale: The Screen Wake Lock API is the perfect mechanism-as-message for a Warhol Sleep re-enactment: a page that refuses sleep literally requests the device not to sleep, and the visibility-gated vigil counter turns the user's attention into the work's medium. Concept and execution collapse cleanly (P1), the readymade is a device API (P2), restraint is honored (P3), and live/no-storage fits the DNA (P4). Tonal control is dry and cheerful-cynic; the small loss-of-support branch ('your browser withholds the vigil') echoes Vanitas/Battery without being derivative. The vignette is materially distinct from the catalogue.
reservations: The pixel-grain/per-frame reseed is a bit busy and could read as 'AI/tech demo' rather than Warhol's flat projection-feel; the breathing ellipse is a small departure from Warhol's figurative subject, replaced here by a luminous mound. The (date, e.g. 2026) on the rights line should be confirmed; otherwise ethics are clean.
revision_suggestion: Consider darkening/desaturating the per-frame grain and slowing the reel-flicker so the loop reads as projection stillness rather than effect; optionally let the sleeper occasionally shift silhouette (arm, turn of head) per minute so five hours feels inhabited without adding storage.
